title: Use an editable curve profile for a flattened path assembly

reference_issue: circular curve bevel does not match a visibly flattened cross-section

action_policy: Use a curve path only when the assembly's primary identity is its editable centerline/path.
Author a separate closed curve profile at the required cross-section aspect ratio.
Assign it as the path's bevel object and hide the profile object from viewport/render output.
Keep both path and profile unapplied; inspect the combined solid diagnostic before accepting the shape.
failure_predicates: a circular bevel depth is used for an observed flattened or rectangular molded section
the profile curve is visible as unintended scene geometry
the path is converted to mesh before silhouette and cross-section are verified
recovery: adjust profile width/height or path points separately, then rerender the combined assembly
replace the curve strategy with an edit-mode mesh cage if the component's cross-section changes incompatibly along its path

evidence.result: PASS: an editable Bézier handle path accepts a hidden closed profile curve through the typed runtime and renders as a flattened cross-section.

promotion_limit: One real-reference repair exercise. It proves runtime support and an editable construction alternative, not final reference likeness or general curve-profile quality.
